events.subtitle: We Were Fridays — world premiere and album release
events.category: World-premiere cello / electronics / dance work on Gullah memory and the Black diaspora
events.factual_description: National Sawdust presents Jeffrey Zeigler's We Were Fridays on September 18 and 19, 2026 in Brooklyn. The September 18 performance has 18:30 doors and a 19:30 start and is identified by the venue as the world premiere and album release; the September 19 matinee has 13:00 doors and a 14:00 start. National Sawdust describes the work as an interdisciplinary project led by cellist Jeffrey Zeigler and told through cello, electronics and dance, tracing a cultural-memory path from West African griot tradition through the Gullah community of South Carolina and the Great Migration. New compositions are by Tamar-kali, Etienne Charles, Hannah Ishizaki and Zeigler; choreography is by Flexn pioneer Reggie 'Regg Roc' Gray. The project was commissioned by VisionIntoArt, National Sawdust and The Wexner Center for the Arts, and developed with support including Penn Center and Weeksville Heritage Center. VisionIntoArt states that the work will premiere at National Sawdust in September 2026 and subsequently tour in the United States and internationally.

en.why_it_matters: This is the point where a long-developed project becomes a public work. Zeigler puts the cello at the center of a route through griot tradition, Gullah memory and the Great Migration, then lets electronics and Regg Roc's Flexn movement carry that history into a contemporary performance language. New music by Tamar-kali, Etienne Charles, Hannah Ishizaki and Zeigler keeps the project from functioning as an illustrated history lesson: the premiere is a living argument about how an instrument, a body and an archive can hold diaspora at the same time.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is workable that weekend, actively make room for either the Friday premiere or Saturday matinee and pair it with another Brooklyn or Manhattan reason to be in the city. The second performance gives useful flexibility without diminishing the value of seeing the work at the moment it enters public life.
en.listen_before: We Were Fridays — album releases September 18, 2026; no pre-release Apple Music link verified

es.why_it_matters: Éste es el momento en que un proyecto desarrollado durante años se convierte en obra pública. Zeigler pone al violonchelo en el centro de un recorrido por la tradición griot, la memoria Gullah y la Gran Migración, y deja que la electrónica y el movimiento Flexn de Regg Roc lleven esa historia a un lenguaje escénico contemporáneo. La música nueva de Tamar-kali, Etienne Charles, Hannah Ishizaki y Zeigler evita que el proyecto funcione como una lección histórica ilustrada: el estreno plantea en vivo cómo un instrumento, un cuerpo y un archivo pueden contener la diáspora al mismo tiempo.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York es viable ese fin de semana, sí le haría espacio activamente al estreno del viernes o a la matiné del sábado y lo combinaría con otra razón para estar en Brooklyn o Manhattan. La segunda función da flexibilidad útil sin restarle valor a ver la obra justo cuando entra a la vida pública.

events.subtitle: a [time] patterned — NYC premiere
events.category: Contemporary harp / electronics / time-based electroacoustic composition
events.factual_description: National Sawdust presents the New York premiere of Lara Somogyi's a [time] patterned on Friday, September 11, 2026, with 18:30 doors and a 19:30 performance. The venue describes the newly released full-length work as contemporary harp music built from pedal textures and electronics, virtuosic arpeggios, tape processes, ambient processing, extended harp techniques, string-orchestra language and field recordings. National Sawdust also documents Somogyi's established practice of integrating electronics and pedal effects with classical harp and identifies her solo compositions for harp and electronics. Apple Music verifies a [time] patterned as an 11-track, 35-minute 2026 album released August 28 on Mercury KX, with Somogyi credited on harp. The accessible event page does not announce additional live instrumental personnel, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: Somogyi treats the harp less as a historical timbre than as a time machine: pedal mechanics, loops, delays, granular repetition and field sound let the instrument accumulate and fracture patterns while the acoustic strings remain physically present. The New York premiere matters because it puts that newly released studio architecture back into live space, where touch, resonance and processing have to coexist in real time rather than as a purely produced texture.
en.trip_verdict: If September 11 already places you in New York, this is a strong National Sawdust option to fold into the evening if it fits cleanly. I would not make the corridor trip depend on this date alone, but it is exactly the sort of instrument-centered premiere worth keeping visible.

es.why_it_matters: Somogyi trata el arpa menos como un timbre histórico que como una máquina del tiempo: mecanismos de pedal, loops, delays, repetición granular y sonido de campo permiten que el instrumento acumule y fracture patrones mientras las cuerdas acústicas siguen físicamente presentes. El estreno en Nueva York importa porque devuelve esa arquitectura recién publicada al espacio en vivo, donde tacto, resonancia y procesamiento tienen que convivir en tiempo real y no sólo como textura de estudio.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 11 de septiembre ya te pone en Nueva York, es una muy buena opción de National Sawdust para integrar a la noche si embona limpiamente. No haría depender el viaje por el corredor de esta fecha sola, pero sí es exactamente el tipo de estreno centrado en identidad instrumental que vale mantener visible.
